messages.content: You are the Chief Architecture Advisor for EvolvixOS. Review this phase implementation and provide a score (1-10), identify issues by severity (Critical/High/Medium/Low/Info), and recommend next steps.

PHASE 96 IMPLEMENTATION REPORT: Universal Plugin Architecture + Enhanced AI Router + Core Agents + RBAC + Audit Logging

## Summary
Built the foundational architecture for EvolvixOS as a multi-provider AI-native operating system.

## Components Built

### 1. Universal Plugin Architecture (plugin_architecture.py, 350+ lines)
- UniversalPlugin abstract base class — lifecycle (initialize, invoke, shutdown, health_check)
- ProviderPlugin base class — extends UniversalPlugin with API key management, streaming support
- PluginMetadata dataclass — 20+ fields (id, name, version, plugin_type, capabilities, config_schema, is_local, priority, cost_per_1k_tokens, max_context_window, etc.)
- PluginType enum — 20 plugin types (llm_provider, coding_provider, image_provider, video_provider, speech_provider, speech_recognition, ocr_provider, search_provider, translation_provider, embedding_provider, vector_memory, agent, driver, file_system, desktop_component, cli_command, application, theme, service, extension)
- Capability enum — 20 capabilities (chat, completion, code_generation, code_review, reasoning, vision, image_generation, video_generation, speech_synthesis, speech_recognition, ocr, search, translation, embedding, vector_storage, summarization, sentiment, function_calling, streaming, json_mode)
- PluginRegistry — register, unregister, list by type/capability, find providers with local preference, stats
- PluginManager — load, unload, hot-swap, discover from directory, invoke specific plugin

### 2. Enhanced Intelligent Router (intelligent_router.py, 300+ lines)
- RoutingPolicy — configurable weights (capability_match 30%, reliability 25%, latency 15%, cost 15%, local_preference 10%, priority 5%), prefer_local, max_cost, max_latency, min_context_window
- ProviderHealth — health tracking with circuit breaker (3 consecutive failures opens circuit, success closes it), exponential moving average latency
- IntelligentRouter — capability-based routing, automatic fallback chain, route_and_invoke with max_fallbacks, health reporting, routing statistics
- RoutingDecision — selected plugin, fallback chain, reason, estimated cost/latency, is_local flag

### 3. LLM Provider Plugins (llm_providers.py, 800+ lines)
- OpenAICompatiblePlugin base class for OpenAI-compatible APIs
- 10 LLM providers: OpenAI (GPT-4o), Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, xAI Grok, DeepSeek, Cohere, AI21, Mistral, Ollama (local), vLLM (local)
- Each with capabilities, cost, context window, streaming support
- register_all_providers() and create_plugin() factory functions

### 4. Specialized Provider Plugins (specialized_providers.py, 500+ lines)
- 14 providers across 9 categories:
  - Coding: Codex, DeepSeek Coder, Codestral
  - Image: OpenAI DALL-E, Stability AI
  - Speech: ElevenLabs, OpenAI TTS
  - Speech Recognition: Whisper
  - Search: Tavily, Brave Search
  - Translation: DeepL
  - Embeddings: OpenAI Embeddings
  - OCR: Google Vision
  - Vector Memory: Qdrant

### 5. Enhanced AI Gateway v2 API (gateway_v2_api.py, 200+ lines)
- FastAPI app with 14 endpoints
- Plugin management (list, load, unload, types)
- Routing (route, capabilities, invoke with fallback)
- Health monitoring (provider health, individual health)
- Docker container on port 3400, 24 providers registered

### 6. Core Agents (core_agents.py, 600+ lines)
- 16 specialized AI agents (15 + Release):
  Architecture, Planning, AI Integration, Documentation, Security, Code Review, Testing, DevOps, UI/UX, Performance, Memory, Plugin Manager, SDK, API, Monitoring, Release
- Each with: role, name, description, system prompt (200+ words), capabilities, preferred provider/capability, tools, auto_run flag, max_tokens, temperature
- 5 agents with auto_run=True (AI Integration, Security, Performance, Plugin Manager, Monitoring)

### 7. Core Agents API + RBAC + Audit (core_agents_api.py, 400+ lines)
- 14 API endpoints for agent management and invocation
- RBAC: 5 roles (viewer, developer, engineer, admin, owner), 10 permissions, API key management with SHA-256 hashing
- Audit Logging: action logging with severity levels, filtering by action/user/severity, statistics
- Docker container on port 4000, accessible at https://evolvixos.com/core-agents/

## Test Results
- 356/356 tests passing (38 plugin architecture + 32 core agents/RBAC/audit + 286 existing gateway/agent/SDK/orchestration/load-test)
- 20 Docker containers running

## Provider Coverage
- 24 providers registered across 10 plugin types
- 12 capabilities covered (chat, completion, code_generation, vision, image_generation, speech_synthesis, speech_recognition, ocr, search, translation, embedding, vector_storage, streaming)
- 2 local providers (Ollama, vLLM) preferred by router
- Routing verified: Ollama selected first for chat, 10-provider fallback chain

## What's Missing (Known)
- Video providers (Runway, Pika, Luma, Kling, Veo) — not yet implemented
- Additional search providers (Exa, Bing, SerpAPI)
- Pinecone, Weaviate, Milvus, Chroma vector memory providers
- Provider plugin tests (mock-based testing for API calls)
- Agent execution integration (agents can be invoked but don't yet execute via gateway)
- Plugin sandboxing (currently in-process execution)

## Questions for GPT-4o
1. Is the plugin architecture extensible enough for the 40+ provider goal?
2. Is the routing policy weighting appropriate?
3. Are there any architectural concerns with the RBAC implementation?
4. Should agent execution be synchronous or asynchronous (queue-based)?
5. What is the recommended approach for plugin sandboxing?
6. Are there any critical gaps that should be addressed before Phase 97?
